title: ephor project manifest (ephor.json)
description: What a project may offer ephor, placed as 'ephor.json' at the forest root (FS-006-project-interface.2). Offered, never required: every field is optional, an empty object is valid, and nothing here gates a capability that probing or site configuration could not establish alone. Resolution is always site configuration over manifest over probe (REQ-001-boundary.2). Identity fields are hints the registry row adopts unless it overrides — the row is authoritative. Commands run relative to the forest root with the trust the person extends to the project's own build; the row's trust switch can narrow this to descriptions only.

identity.description: Hints for attribution (FS-008-attribution.1). Adopted by the registry row, never overriding it.

ticket_patterns.description: Regular expressions matching the project's ticket keys, e.g. 'GR-\\d+'.

repos.description: The forest's repositories as the forge names them (owner/name or slug).

territory.description: Repositories and organizations that are this project's business without being in its forest — 'owner/name', or 'owner/*' for an organization. Places general mentions, stray issues, adjacent discussions (FS-008-attribution.1).

addresses.description: Mail addresses and lists whose conversations belong to this project.

main.description: The main branch this repository trails (default: the project's).

forest.description: The forest's own layout (AR-004-forest). The registry row overrides paths and remotes for where things sit on a particular machine.

checks.description: Check verbs (FS-006-project-interface.5), overriding the probed ./check.sh, ./check-style.sh, ./smoke-test.sh. Each script is self-contained: a smoke test that needs a build performs its build.

oneOf.description: Discover by running the command with --list; it prints one feature id per line, or a features[] envelope.

ci.description: Gate verbs (FS-006-project-interface.6) — project truth, the same for every developer; site configuration overrides for credentials or variants. Each is a summons: EPHOR_* environment in (EPHOR_REPO, EPHOR_NUMBER, EPHOR_BRANCH name the matter), exit code plus $EPHOR_ANSWER envelope out. status answers gate; failures answers failures[]; restart re-runs the failing gate and everything downstream of it, committing nothing (FS-005-dispatch.11), exit 75 meaning 'still running, ask again later'.

kind.description: 'rhei', 'beads', or another store ephor has a reader for.

tickets.description: Local ticket stores beyond the probed conventions (FS-006-project-interface.7).

actions.description: The project's offers (FS-006-project-interface.9): menu entries beside the person's own, person's same-id entries winning. Invoked by a person, run as a summons, gated by 'requires'.

command.description: A command line run via sh -c in the resolved place (FS-006-project-interface.3).

feature.description: One feature a smoke test can run alone. The same shape the answer envelope uses, spelled here too so this schema validates offline (FS-006-project-interface.11).

paths.description: Globs relating the feature to source paths, for change-driven selection.

requires.description: Capability rungs this offer needs (FS-006-project-interface.10); unmet rungs render '(unavailable: …)'.

selector.description: The shared offer/recipe selector language (FS-006-project-interface.9): the same fields a work recipe's 'when' takes, so one language selects both. Every stated field must hold; a field left out asks nothing.

kinds.description: Item kinds as ephor spells them; 'message' is accepted for 'msg'.

behind.description: The matter's branch trails its main branch (true) or is level with it (false), measured in the checkout. An unmeasurable checkout matches neither (FS-004-quick-actions.6).

behind_upstream.description: The matter's branch trails its own published copy (true) or is level with it (false), measured in the checkout. A branch published nowhere matches neither (FS-004-quick-actions.8).
